record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For n ≥ 2, can one find a smooth compact connected hypersurface M^{2n−1} ⊂ R^{2n} whose characteristic flow is minimal, meaning that every orbit is dense in M^{2n−1}?

evidence.quote: 1. When n≥ 2 can one ﬁnd M 2n−1⊂ R2n, a C∞ -compact connected hypersurface, such that on M 2n−1 the characteristic ﬂow is minimal (every orbit is dense) ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$. Consider $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ equipped with the standard symplectic form $\omega = \sum_{i=1}^n dx_i \wedge dy_i$. For a smooth compact connected hypersurface $M \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ (so $\dim M = 2n-1$), the characteristic line field on $M$ is the kernel of the restriction $\omega|_M$; at each $p \in M$ this is a 1-dimensional subspace of $T_pM$. Any nowhere-vanishing smooth vector field spanning this line field generates the characteristic flow on $M$ (well-defined up to time reparametrization), and its orbits are the leaves of the characteristic foliation.

The characteristic flow is called minimal if every one of its orbits is dense in $M$.

Question: Does there exist, for some $n \geq 2$, a smooth compact connected hypersurface $M^{2n-1} \subset \mathbb{R}^{2n}$ whose characteristic flow is minimal?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of finding a smooth compact hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ ($n\geq 2$) whose characteristic flow is minimal does not appear to have been resolved. Related work concerns hypersurfaces without closed characteristics (Hermann, Ginzburg) and contact-type cases (Weinstein conjecture, Viterbo), but no construction or obstruction for a minimal characteristic flow on a compact hypersurface in Euclidean space appears in the standard literature.

status_evidence.title: Robustly Non-Convex Hypersurfaces in Contact Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Dynamics of characteristic foliations on hypersurfaces; recent work explores heterodimensional cycles but minimality on Euclidean hypersurfaces is not established.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies characteristic foliation dynamics but does not provide a minimal example or obstruction in $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$.

status_evidence.title: The existence of two closed characteristics on every compact star-shaped hypersurface in R^4
status_evidence.snippet: Existence results for closed characteristics on compact hypersurfaces in R^4.
status_evidence.claim: Research focuses on existence of closed orbits; the complementary question of complete minimality remains unresolved.
